findings.description: Goal F7's acceptance criterion (docs/planning/v1.2.md section 2) requires 'ADR-009 and ADR-002/ADR-003 amendment notes are recorded'. Task 20.3 recorded the ADR-009 and ADR-003 amendment notes (and updated their decisions-index rows) but recorded no ADR-002 note, and the ADR-002 index row still reads bare 'Accepted'. ADR-024 clause 8 and its status line extend 'the ADR-002/ADR-003 restoration trigger set', and ADR-002 is precisely the ADR that defines that trigger set (disable/uninstall enters RestorePending, a present baseline is restored, an absent baseline is removed, item removal enters Removed). A reader of ADR-002 alone therefore still sees the pre-v1.2 trigger set. The omission originates in the plan of record: PLANS.md Phase 20 deliverables ('ADR-024 plus ADR-009 and ADR-003 amendment notes') and the v1.2 section 7 documentation checklist ('ADR-009.md and ADR-003.md (supersession/extension notes)') both drop ADR-002, so the planner's task set inherited a narrower list than the F7 goal criterion states.

observations.proposed_change: .opencode/agents/orchestrator.md (Worker Delegation section): instruct that a task delegation must not quote absolute historical suite totals; require the worker to measure and state its own pre-change baseline, and if a count is quoted it must be generated from the current tree immediately before dispatch.
observations.rationale: A stale delegated baseline is a small but repeated source of confusion: the worker prompt treats the stated baseline as the consistency anchor, so a stale value pushes every task to spend time reconciling delegation text against reality. Removing absolute counts from delegations costs nothing and eliminates the mismatch.

observations.proposed_change: .opencode/scripts/collect-session-usage.sh: replace the `opencode api get` call in api_get() with a direct HTTP request (for example `curl -fsS`) to the resolved server URL's /api/session/<id> endpoint, keeping the existing OPENCODE_SERVER/port discovery, so metadata collection does not depend on the broken `opencode` CLI.
observations.rationale: The orchestrator prompt makes the wrapper the authoritative path and forbids estimation; if the wrapper silently depends on a broken CLI, every task forces a manual alternative and raises the risk that a future orchestrator records nulls instead of real values. A curl-based read of the same endpoint keeps the authoritative source while removing the CLI dependency.

summary: Phase 20 (Empty-selection artwork restoration, Goal F7, ADR-024) is complete and the gate can be applied. All three tasks in the authoritative execution order (20.1, 20.2, 20.3) are done with a commit, a worker report, an APPROVED implementation review, a PASS_WITH_FINDINGS test-quality review, and a per-invocation orchestration record; the phase-level aggregate exists and its sums are exact. There were no correction rounds and no BLOCKED/FAILED/NEEDS_RESEARCH invocation; implementation reviews approved on attempt 1 (3/3) and the test-quality reviews' LOW/INFORMATIONAL residuals were closed or honestly carried. I independently rebuilt the tree, reran the F7-focused classes (103 passed / 4 skipped / 107) and the full default suite (Failed 0 / Passed 1927 / Skipped 66 / Total 1993), and ran check-docs.sh (PASS). Architecturally the phase stays inside the documented boundaries: the discriminator is single-sourced (NoDisplayableValue only for an empty resolved selection at SkiaBadgeRenderer.cs:85; NoFittingBadge only for a non-empty layout-empty selection at :230), the only restore entry point is the pre-existing internal ArtworkPublisher.RestoreAsync, no subject-gate reentrancy or deadlock path exists, the absent-baseline leg is correctly attributed to the publisher (not coordinator) in the corrected architecture text, and no RenderVersion/schema/fingerprint/golden changed. Platform assumptions are bounded and honest: the save/remove ABI was pinned in task 5.1 and live-verified in task 14.3, native NoFittingBadge cases run only under ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT=1, and no live host run is part of this phase. The pre-gate phase state is correct: Phase 20 is still PLANNED in state.json and PLANS.md with no v1.2.0-phase20 tag and no gate_record. Two findings remain, neither blocking: PR-20-01 (MEDIUM) - the Goal F7 criterion names an ADR-002 amendment note that was not recorded (the plan's own Phase 20 deliverable list drops ADR-002), so ADR-002 and its index row still show only the pre-v1.2 restoration trigger set; PR-20-02 (LOW) - the phase aggregate's note references a phase-reviewer section the draft does not contain. The gate text is the plan's Gate 20 verbatim, unamended, and the delivered result does not weaken it. APPROVED_WITH_FINDINGS; ready for the next phase.
